text: She reached the top of the ridge and the canyon opened beneath her all at once, layer after layer of red rock falling away for miles until the river at the bottom was only a thin silver thread
He lay on his back in the desert far from any town and the Milky Way stretched from one horizon to the other so thick with stars that it looked like spilled flour across black cloth
The whale surfaced twenty feet from the boat and its back kept rising and rising out of the water, longer than the boat itself, and then it exhaled and the spray drifted over them like warm rain
The nurse placed the baby on her chest and she looked down at the tiny fingers curling around her own and realized that an hour ago this person had not existed anywhere in the world

He walked into the cathedral and his eyes went up the stone columns to the vaulted ceiling a hundred feet overhead, and the light from the rose window fell in colored shafts through the dust in the air
The northern lights started as a faint green smudge and then spread across the whole sky in rippling curtains that folded and unfolded over the frozen lake while nobody in the group said a word

She stood at the base of the redwood and tipped her head back and still could not see the top, the trunk rising past the lower branches into a canopy that had been growing since before the printing press
When the orchestra came in all at once after the long quiet passage, the sound hit him in the chest like a wave and the hair stood up on his arms and he forgot he was sitting in a seat

The eclipse reached totality and the temperature dropped and the birds went silent and where the sun had been there was a black disk ringed in white fire, and stars appeared in the middle of the afternoon

He looked through the telescope at the faint smudge of light and the astronomer told him it was a galaxy, two hundred billion suns, and the light entering his eye had left it before there were people on Earth
The glacier calved with a crack like a cannon and a wall of blue ice the size of an apartment building slid into the fjord and the wave rolled out toward their kayaks long seconds later

She looked through the microscope at a single drop of pond water and it was full of life, translucent creatures spinning and pulsing and feeding, a whole crowded world she had been walking past her entire life

The plane broke through the clouds and below them the Himalayas rose out of the white like the backs of enormous animals, their peaks catching the first sunlight while the valleys were still in shadow

He stood in front of the waterfall and the roar filled everything and the mist soaked his clothes and the ground under his feet trembled with the weight of the water falling and falling without ever running out

The choir of three hundred voices held the final chord and it rang off the stone walls and kept ringing after they had stopped, hanging in the air above the audience for what seemed like a full minute

She watched the rocket lift off from three miles away and the light came first, brighter than the sun, and then the sound arrived and shook her ribs and the car alarms in the parking lot all went off at once

The storm came across the plains as a single black wall a hundred miles wide, lightning flickering inside it constantly, and he pulled the truck over just to watch the sky go from blue to green to night

He walked out of the museum hall and into the room with the blue whale skeleton suspended from the ceiling, and he had to keep walking to get from the tail to the skull, and he stopped and just stood under the ribs
The murmuration rose from the reeds at dusk, tens of thousands of starlings moving as one shape, stretching and folding and pouring across the sky like smoke that had decided where to go

She held the fossil in her palm, a perfect spiral shell turned to stone, and the geologist said the animal had been alive in a warm sea here three hundred million years ago where there was now a cornfield

The ship left the harbor and after three days there was no land in any direction, just water meeting sky in a perfect circle all around him, and at night the darkness was so total the stars came right down to the waves
The old pianist played the piece from memory with her eyes closed, her hands moving faster than he could follow, and he could not understand how a human body had learned to do this
He stood at the edge of the volcano crater at night and far below the lava lake churned orange and black, splitting open and sealing over, the ground warm through the soles of his boots
The diver hung motionless in the clear water as the manta ray glided over her, its wings blotting out the sunlight, so close she could see its gills open and close as it passed without a sound

She saw the earthrise photograph for the first time as a child, the blue and white planet hanging over the gray horizon of the moon, and understood suddenly that everyone she had ever known was on that one small ball
The fireflies came up out of the meadow all at once at dusk, thousands of them, blinking in waves that rolled across the field in unison until the whole valley was pulsing with cold green light

He walked between the stones of the ancient circle at sunrise and the light came through the gap exactly where the builders had placed it five thousand years ago, landing on the altar stone like a key turning in a lock

The surgeon showed her the scan of her own heart on the screen, the valves opening and closing in perfect rhythm, and she realized it had been doing this every second of her life without her ever asking it to
From the summit at dawn the shadow of the mountain stretched out across the clouds below as a perfect dark triangle reaching all the way to the horizon
The migrating herd crossed the plain below the ridge and it took the entire afternoon, an unbroken river of wildebeest flowing past, the dust rising in a cloud that turned gold in the setting sun

He stepped into the cave and turned off his headlamp and the ceiling above him lit up with thousands of glowworms, blue-green points of light spread across the rock like a second night sky underground
She stood at the foot of the dam and looked up at the curved concrete wall rising seven hundred feet, holding back an entire lake, and thought about the people who had poured it by hand

The thunderstorm passed and a double rainbow appeared over the valley, both arcs complete from end to end, the sky between them darker than the sky outside, and everyone on the street stopped and turned to look
He read the equation on the chalkboard, just a few symbols, and the professor explained that it described how every planet and every falling apple moved, and the whole room went quiet

The ice on the lake was so clear and black that when she lay on it she could see straight down through three feet of ice to the stones and weeds on the bottom, the cracks below her singing in long eerie tones

From the window of the airplane at night he saw the whole coastline traced in lights, city after city connected by glowing threads of highway, millions of people each living their own entire life down there

The salt flats went on in every direction, perfectly flat and perfectly white, and after the rain a thin layer of water turned the ground into a mirror so that she seemed to be standing in the middle of the sky

The sequoia grove was silent except for the wind high above, and he put his hand flat against the bark of the oldest tree and felt how the trunk did not move at all, as if it were part of the mountain
The tidal bore came up the river as a single wave stretching from bank to bank, a wall of brown water moving upstream against the current, and the sound arrived before they could see it

She opened the old family Bible and found the names written on the inside cover, generation after generation in different handwriting going back two hundred years, each one a person whose life had led to hers
